input.reasoning_summary:
After investigating potential challenges to the initial verdict, I find no evidence that would weaken or overturn it.

H1 (One-time charges/unusual items): The counter-evidence retrieved (E7, E8, E9) does not mention any one-time charges, restructuring costs, or unusual items affecting Q3 FY2026 subscription costs. E7 shows the standard cost breakdown with "Various individually insignificant items" contributing only 2% to the change. There is no indication that the 22% contribution from hosting and data center costs was inflated by temporary or non-recurring factors.

H2 (Acquisitions/business changes): While E11 mentions the acquisition of Semrush in April 2026, this is discussed in the context of enhancing Adobe Experience Manager offerings and revenue growth, not in relation to cost of subscription revenue. The evidence does not indicate that this acquisition distorted the cost comparison or affected the attribution of hosting and data center costs as the main driver. E10 and E12 discuss customer-focused strategy but provide no evidence of cost structure changes affecting the claim.

H3 (Accounting changes): The counter-evidence (E13, E14, E15) shows consistent definitions and descriptions of cost of subscription revenue components across different periods. There is no mention of any changes in cost allocation methodology or accounting treatment between Q3 FY2025 and Q3 FY2026 that would make the comparison misleading.

The original supporting evidence (E3 and E6) remains valid and directly supports the claim. E3 explicitly states that hosting services and data center costs were the primary driver (22 percentage points out of 24% total increase) for Q3 FY2026, and E6 confirms the overall increase in cost of subscription revenue for that period.
